prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively pick a single “best” roofer for Denver without knowing your exact location and priorities, but I can help you find the right contractor and avoid common scams. If you tell me your ZIP code (or upload photos of the damage), I can build a short, vetted list of local roofers and sample questions to ask them. Meanwhile, here’s a practical checklist and what to look for.

How to choose the best roofer for hail damage
- Get at least 3 written estimates after an on-site inspection.
- Prefer roofers who handle insurance claims and will meet your adjuster on site.
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp, Angi), BBB ratings, and recent local references (ask for addresses of recent hail repairs).
- Verify insurance and licensing: confirm the company carries liability and workers’ comp insurance; confirm any local contractor registration required by Denver.
- Look for manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) — these support extended warranties.
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer shingle warranty and a contractor workmanship warranty (get both in writing).
- Confirm they pull required permits and handle cleanup and disposal.

Questions to ask every roofer
- Are you licensed/registered to work in Denver, and can you provide your registration number and proof of insurance?
- Do you have experience with insurance claims for hail damage? Will you meet my insurance adjuster?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and photos of completed jobs?
- What brands of shingles do you install, and are you a certified installer for those brands?
- What warranties do you provide (manufacturer + workmanship) and are they written?
- What is the estimated start and completion timeline, and what is the payment schedule?
- Do you handle permits and disposal/cleanup?

Red flags to avoid
- Storm-chasers: roofers who show up right after a storm, pressure you to sign immediately, or ask for large upfront cash.
- No written estimate or vague scope of work.
- Pressure to use the contractor the insurance company recommends exclusively.
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide references.
- Extremely low bid far below others — could be poor materials or subcontracting.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of top-rated Denver roofers (need your ZIP).
- Draft an email/text template to request estimates.
- Help compare 2–3 written estimates if you paste them here.

Which would you like me to do next?
